title: Incremental Typed Frames with Observability Tokens and Safe Tool Handoffs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: PRD to define a deterministic, testable contract for transmitting partially-complete structured outputs as typed frames, carrying inline observability tokens to enable end-to-end tracing, and a safe tool-handshake mechanism that guarantees idempotency and clear error modes for streaming function/tool invocations.
success_metrics: Reduce production schema-parsing errors for streaming responses by >= 80% within first month of rollout
< 1 per 10k tool-invocations resulting in ambiguous idempotency status
Average recovery-to-valid-output time for a transient framing error < 2s with automatic fallback enabled
95% of customer workloads can enable progressive frames without custom SDK changes
requirements: Define a compact envelope format for typed frames (meta, type, sequence_id, partial/complete flag, observability_token, payload) usable in streaming and non-streaming responses
Provide a handshake header that allows caller and callee to negotiate schema strictness (strict|lenient|checkpointed) per-request
Tool invocation must include an idempotency token and a deterministic replay key derived from the request context
Streaming clients must be able to request 'checkpoint' frames that act as stable validation points for resumed parsing
Server must emit machine-readable error categories (validation_error, transient_runtime, tool_unavailable, schema_mismatch) along with remediation hints
All frames must be traceable via an observability_token that maps to existing tracing infrastructure (trace_id/span_id) and is present even for partial frames
SDKs should provide parser helpers that validate frames incrementally and expose typed events to application code
Admin controls in Console to toggle strictness, fallback policies, and retention of partial frames for debugging
out_of_scope: Redesigning non-streamed function-calling semantics for synchronous-only use cases
Major protocol changes to existing hosted API surface (we will add headers but not change top-level endpoints)
Full binary/Protobuf wire format in initial release (JSON-first rollout)
On-prem private deployment custom kernels for frame assembly (defer to runtime team later)
api_contract: Handshake: client may send 'X-RW-Frame-Mode: strict|lenient|checkpointed' and 'X-RW-Tool-Mode: idempotent|best-effort' headers; server responds with 'X-RW-Frame-Mode-Ack' and permitted features
Typed frames: each payload includes a top-level '$schema' URI and an optional '$partial_of' reference for incremental assembly
Checkpoint frames: carry a stable checksum and a validation_status field; once received, SDKs may mark earlier fragments as immutable
Observability tokens: short opaque token that maps 1:1 to trace context; must be present on all frames and tool callbacks
streaming_semantics: Partial payloads are allowed but must include '$partial_of' with a 'total_expected_frames' when known
Frames must be strictly ordered by 'seq' and server guarantees monotonic increments; clients should be tolerant to skipped seq in case of network loss but rely on checkpoint frames to resume
Resume behavior: client supplies last-acknowledged 'seq' to request replay from server; server may re-emit from last checkpoint only
Backpressure: server can emit 'control' frames with 'pause' or 'throttle' directives; SDKs must surface these as flow-control events to application code
Streaming must support interleaving data frames and control frames (e.g., a partial schema frame followed by an observability-only keepalive)
tool_call_behaviors: Tool gateway must respond with a deterministic 'invocation_result_id' to indicate whether a retry is safe or will produce a duplicate effect
On transient errors, client retries must honor exponential backoff capped by 'max_retries' defined in the handshake; retries must provide the same idempotency_key
Fallback policy: if primary tool is unavailable, server may automatically route to a read-only or simulated tool variant when handshake indicates 'best-effort'
Tool responses may be streamed back as frames; the final tool-completion frame must set 'is_complete'=true and include final status codes
error_modes_and_recovery: Validation_error: occurs when a typed frame fails schema validation; server emits an 'error' frame with 'fix_suggestion' and 'affected_seq'
Transient_runtime: temporary compute or I/O failure; server marks frame as 'retryable' and may requeue for serving runtime without client action
Tool_unavailable: tool gateway returns 503-like semantics; if handshake allowed fallback, server must emit 'control' frame announcing fallback and which substitution occurred
Schema_mismatch: client requested strict mode but emitted payload doesn't match; server must either emit a failure 'error' frame or degrade to lenient mode if negotiated
On unrecoverable errors, server emits a terminal 'error' frame and must include 'diagnostic_blob' pointer (kept for 7 days) to aid postmortem
acceptance_criteria: Canonical parser test: Given a stream of mixed data/checkpoint/control frames, SDK parser must reconstruct final JSON when checkpoint signals completion in 99/100 unit tests
Handshake compliance: Server and client exchange headers and agree on frame mode; automated tests validate that server honors 'lenient' and 'strict' modes across 50 randomized schema fuzz runs
Idempotency safety: Simulate duplicate tool invocation with same idempotency_key; only one effective side-effect observed in 1000 simulated runs
Backpressure handling: SDK pauses consumption on 'control:pause' and resumes without data corruption; validated by integration test with artificial throttle
Observability linkage: Each frame in a traced session maps to a single trace_id in telemetry; cross-check via Console traces and SDK logs
Error classification: For each error mode, system emits the correct error frame type and the Console surfaces remediation guidance within 30s
Resume correctness: After network drop at arbitrary seq, client can resume from last checkpoint and produce identical reconstructed payload to a continuous run
Performance guardrail: Enabling progressive frames should not increase median p99 response latency by more than 10% for standard gen workloads
telemetry_and_debugging: Per-frame metrics: frames_emitted_total, frames_failed_validation_total, checkpoint_latency_ms p50/p90/p99
Tool invocation metrics: tool_invocations_total, tool_invocation_retry_rate, tool_invocation_idempotency_conflicts
Traces: include obs_token in all spans and emit an event for handshake, each checkpoint, and tool handoff completion
Debug artifacts: On terminal errors, save last N frames and associated checksum to a diagnostic bucket; surface link in Console error view
Sampling: default sample rate for full-frame payload capture is 0.1% but admin-configurable per-user/org
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal): SDK + server implementation behind feature flag; run against 10 internal services for 3 weeks
Phase 2 (beta): Open to customers on request; provide migration guide and parsing helpers for Node/Python/Go SDKs
Phase 3 (gradual): Default-on for new accounts and opt-in for existing accounts with dashboard toggle; monitor success metrics and rollback on regressions
Phase 4 (GA): Remove feature flag after 8 weeks of stable beta and announce in release notes with examples and integration tests
